author: nadgruaz
body:
* Hi, 

* iba to delete ??   
GO:0042393 | histone binding | ECO:0000318(IBA) | ECO:0000318 | (IBA)

* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**
* DR PANTHER=PTHR19879; TRANSCRIPTION INITIATION FACTOR TFIID; 1
DR PANTHER=PTHR19879:SF9; TRANSCRIPTION INITIATION FACTOR TFIID SUBUNIT 5; 1


* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
*  Q86VZ2 WDR5B

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**

WDR5B did not appear to robustly associate with chromatin under the same experimental
conditions (as WDR5). In vitro binding of WDR5, but not WDR5B, to recombinant nucleosomes also
suggests that WDR5B may exhibit little intrinsic chromatin binding ability. histone binding not confirmed   WDR5B enrichment was not detected at WDR5 genomic binding sites
   PubMed=39056772 

* Add the label 'high priority' if needed. Generally high priority issues affect a lot of proteins, and annotations are incorrect (as opposed to just imprecise).

Many thanks in advance, 
Cheers, 
Nadine
title: IBA to delete Q86VZ2 WDR5B ?

author: marcfeuermann
body: The nodes corresponding to WDR5 and WDR5B are not in PTHR19879 anymore but have moved into PTHR22847. I have completely re-annotated the latter family and the problematic annotations are no more associated with the WDR5B node.
